sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that, present is a case of no evidence.

It is pointed out that, prosecution case in short is that, prosecutrix (PW-1) had presented herself before the Police Center, Tejgarh District Damoh on 21.10.2016 and lodged a report (Ex.P-1) to the effect that, on 20.10.2016 at about 08:00 p.m., she was sleeping with her son.
Her husband had gone to earn his livelihood for last 45 days at Jabera.
Her father- in-law (PW-2) and mother-in-law (PW-4) were sleeping in the room, next to her room in the same house.
Daughter of the prosecutrix was also sleeping with her grand parents.

At about 02:00 a.m., somebody had knocked the door of her house,
she thought that, her husband may have come back and then she had switch on the light and opened the gates.
She found that, Shyam Raikwar (Present appellant) was on her gate.
When she asked Shyam, as to how he had come at such an odd hour, then Shyam thrust himself inside the room.

When prosecutrix tried to shout, then he had pressed her mouth with his hand and threatened her,
thereafter, he violated her privacy.
After sometime, when she shouted, then her in-laws came to the place of the incident.
Her father-in-law had locked the room.
He had called Kotwar Pawan Mehra (PW-5), Govind Prasad (PW-3) and Kallu Mehra (PW-6) and Dialed 100.
When her father-in-law opened the doors of the room in front of other villagers, that time, Shyam had run away, which was seen by the witnesses.

On the basis of the said report, case Crime No. 232 of 2016 was registered under Section 376, 450 & 506 of Indian Penal Code and under NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

sentences.text: 3. It is submitted that, the prosecutrix was a consenting adult.
From the slide (Ex. A) and petticoat (Ex.B) of the prosecutrix 'Y' STR DNA Profile was obtained.

The 'Y' STR DNA Profile obtained from the blood source of Shyam Raikwar as contained in Ex.C depicted all the alleles obtained from the slide of prosecutrix (Ex.A) and petticoat (Ex.B).
4.

Thus, it is submitted that, a consensual relationship between two consenting adults has been turned to be a case of forceful violation of privacy which is not made out from the facts and circumstances of the case.
Conduct of the prosecutrix is unnatural.

It is not possible that, she could not raise an alarm, even when her privacy was violated, because it is not the case of the prosecutrix that, at the time of violation of her privacy or at the time of removal of her cloths, accused still prevented her from raising an alarm.

It is submitted that, in fact when father-in-law of the prosecutrix came to know of this illicit relationship, a case of consensual relationship has been Shyam Raikwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53921144/

sentences.text: 5. Learned, Government Advocate supports the impugned judgment and submits that, no indulgence is called for.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the records, prosecutrix (PW-1)
after making allegation as narrated above, admits in her cross-examination that Shyam is known to her, as he is resident of the same village.
She admits that, she was talking to Shyam.
She further admits in para-4 of her cross-examination that on the date of the incident, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10246 4 CRA-911-2025 she had called Shyam at night to talk to her.
She admits that, when Shyam had entered her room, then somebody had locked it from outside.

Thereafter, she has turned hostile and has not supported the case of the prosecution.
7.
Learned ADPO, declared her hostile and leading questions were put to her.
She admits that, she had entered into a compromise with Shyam.
She stated that, whatever is being stated today, is correct and whatever was stated by her at earlier point of time was incorrect.
She denied that, she was making incorrect statements on account of compromise.
She admits that, she had called Shyam at night in a casual manner and did not disclose for what purpose, she had called Shyam.
8. Father-in-law of the prosecutrix (PW-2) stated that, Police had not taken his statements.
They had only obtained his signatures on 02-03 papers.
This witness was declared hostile.
Leading questions were put to him.
He admits that, prosecutrix and her husband resides by the side of his house.
He admitted that, husband of the prosecutrix had gone to Jabera for earning his livelihood.
He has not supported prosecution case.
He denied that, he had called Dial-100, he had denied that when he had opened the gate of the room of his daughter-in-law, Shyam Raikwar had run from inside the room.
9. Govind Prasad (PW-3) stated accused is not belonging to SC/ST, whereas prosecutrix belongs to SC/ST category.
This witness too was declared hostile.
In cross-examination, this witness admits that, during his interrogation, he had not narrated anything about the accused and the prosecutrix at Police Station.

10. Mother-in-law of the prosecutrix (PW-4) stated that, she has no NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:10246 5 CRA-911-2025 knowledge about the case.
In cross-examination, she admits that, she was not present at the time of the incident in her village.
She admits that, she has no information about the incident.
11. Pawan Kumar Jharia (PW-5) states that, when he had reached the house of prosecutrix, he had not seen anybody nor met anybody.
This witness too was declared hostile, but he has not supported the prosecution case.
In his cross-examination, he admits that, Patwari had prepared Map, prior to his reaching on the spot.
He has no knowledge as to why map was prepared.

He has no knowledge,
as to on what basis, victim had lodged report against Shyam.

sentences.text: Kallu Mehara (PW-6) has also not supported the prosecution case.

Uma Prasad Ahirwar, (PW-7),
ASI (Retd.) stated that, on being given by women Ct. Neha Rai, he had seized the sealed slides and petticoat vide Ex.P-10.
Ramakant Dwivedi (PW-8), Assistant Grade-III, proved the caste certificate of the victim as contained in Ex.P-11.

Dashrath Prasad Dubey (PW-9), Sub-Inspector, stated that,
victim had lodged a report, which was recorded by him registering Case Crime No.232 of 2016.

Dr.
P.C. Swarnkar (PW-10) had drawn samples of the accused for DNA Examination.
Women Ct. Neha Rahi (PW-11) had taken the victim to the lady Doctor for examination.

Dr. Seema Patel (PW-12) had examined the victim stated that, she had not seen any injury mark,
either external or internal.
Her hymen was torn.
Prosecutrix had two children from her previous deliveries which were normal, there were no signs of use of force.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10246 6 CRA-911-2025 14.
Dy. S.P., Mukesh Abidra (PW-13) had conducted investigation.
He admits that Ex.P-1 contains the signature of the prosecutrix, he admits that statements of the prosecutrix and other witnesses are not in his handwriting.
He admits that, these statements were not read over to the prosecutrix.

15. When all facts are taken into consideration, especially the evidence of the prosecutrix, it is evident that once prosecutrix admits that, she had herself called the appellant to her home, that too at 02:00 a.m. and then she did not raise any alarm, whereas somebody had locked the house from outside, and prosecution witnesses have not supported the prosecution case, then positivity of DNA Report (Ex.P-18) proves that, privacy of the prosecutrix was violated.

16. However, circumstances obtaining in the case especially as narrated by the Lady Doctor (PW-12)
Dr. Seem Patel that there were no injury marks, there was no evidence of any use of force and looking to the fact that, prosecutrix herself admits that she was undressed by the accused, her privacy was violated, yet she had not raised any alarm, leaves no iota of doubt that, prosecutrix was a consenting party and therefore, when this fact is taken into consideration, then in the matter of consent between two consenting adults, there being no use of force or coercion, conviction of the appellant cannot be sustained in the eyes of law as it will not fall withing the definition of 'rape' as defined in Section 375 of Indian Penal Code.
17.
Accordingly, impugned judgment of conviction needs to be set- aside and is hereby set-aside.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10246 7 CRA-911-2025 18.
In the result this Criminal Appeal is allowed and disposed of.
Appellant is in jail, be released forthwith, if not required in any other offence.
19. Record of the learned trial Court be sent back.
20. Consequently, all the pending Interlocutory Applications be disposed of.
(VIVEK AGARWAL)
